diagnosis: Every unit waits at its home post; the closest idle unit is sent.

Under the baseline every unit sits at its home post, so the west and south side (Sunset/Parkside, Outer Richmond, Inner Sunset, Excelsior, Visitacion Valley, Lakeshore) is covered by units stationed in the central and eastern posts. The worst calls there show closest-post drives of 350-500 s, and the unit sent often came from posts 0, 2 or 5. I replaced the fixed layout with an hourly demand-weighted coverage plan: for each time bucket, posts are chosen greedily to minimize drive time to demand, with extra weight on the west and south posts and a penalty on long drives. On-shift units are then matched to the chosen posts by shortest relocation. I have not run the simulator, so the effect on the slow-neighborhood median and the 5 s citywide limit is untested.

Sunset/Parkside (post 22), Outer Richmond/Lincoln Park (post 31) and Excelsior (post 40) are served from the stacked central posts 0 and 2, so calls there show 900-1000 s drives against 360-450 s from the local post. I moved up to 3 spare on-shift units from the most crowded posts to posts 22, 40 and 31 and left everything else alone. I haven't run the simulator, so the effect on the slow-neighborhood median and the 5 s citywide limit is untested.
